plan.name: A deployed service is placed in its declared container
plan.rationale: A deployed-in relationship in the architecture model says where a service runs. Without a placement fact in the manifests of each environment, the model states something that the deployment definition does not show.
plan.remediation: Place a workload of the service in the hosting target (the namespace) that is bound to the declared container, in every environment. When the manifests are templated or outside the environment sources, supply the evidence or bind the workload and the namespace.

plan.name: A deployed service has no unexpected placement
plan.rationale: A workload that is placed in a hosting target other than the declared container, or a placement in the reverse direction, contradicts the deployed-in relationship of the architecture model. It is reported apart from the missing placement of INFRA-PLC-001.
plan.remediation: Move the workload to the declared container, or change the deployed-in relationship in the architecture model. If the hosting target has no binding, bind it to the architecture node it belongs to.

plan.remediation: Write the image reference of each container in the manifest, or render the template so that the reference is a literal. Concordia never guesses an image.

plan.name: Each image of a deployable service has a build definition candidate
plan.rationale: A build definition links an image to its source. The link exists only when a build command names the image, so an absence is never a definite violation and a link that is present is a candidate.
plan.remediation: Name the image in a build command (for example docker build -t) that the index can read, or bind the image of a third-party service as not built here by leaving it without an image binding.
